g.text: 4 · Eight rings, staggered by 1.6 nm = FSR/8 → cyclic

text.style: font-size: 8.4px; font-family: 'Inter', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #f6f6f6

g.text: Rings differ slightly in circumference, so their resonances split one FSR into 8 equal steps;

text.style: font-size: 8.4px; font-family: 'Inter', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #f6f6f6

g.text: after ring 8, ring 1’s next resonance comes round → any ring can take the nearest channel → minimum heating.

text.style: font-style: italic; font-size: 7.2px; font-family: 'Inter', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: end; fill: #a1a1a6

g.text: computed: book ring eq., Q = 5000; dip depth illustrative

g.text: Takeaway: 7.5 µm rib rings (FSR 12.8 nm), mostly pn-doped, Q lowered to 5000 by a 2nd bus → 35 GHz; a heater tunes; 8 × 1.6 nm = one FSR.

text.style: font-size: 7.9px; font-family: 'Inter', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: middle; fill: #a1a1a6

g.text: Book Sec. 13.1.2 (p. 408). Panels 3–4 computed here with the book’s ring equations (Eq. 4.27, 6.17–6.21), λ ≈ 1550 nm assumed — not measured data.
